newsitem.title: USA: Niagara Mohawk to terminate NYPA contract.
newsitem.headline: Niagara Mohawk to terminate NYPA contract.

text.p: Niagara Mohawk Power Corp said Tuesday it will terminate an uneconomic contract with the New York Power Authority on May 24.
The utility also said it will ask the Public Service Commission for permission to provide electricity at a discounted price to those customers affected by the cancellation of the NYPA contract.

The two-part contract calls for Niagara Mohawk to purchase electricity from NYPA's Fitzpatrick plant at an above-market price and to wheel additional power from that plant to certain industrial customers.
Niagara Mohawk spokeswoman Kerry P. Burns said 87 megawatts of power are involved in the contract.
The NYPA contract, which was originally signed in 1975, was amended several times over the years, the utility said.

The commission concluded the contract was uneconomic in a 1995 order. After several attempts to negotiate a new contract failed, Niagara Mohawk exercised its termination right. The company notified NYPA on May 24, 1996, that the contract would be canceled a year later.
Tuesday, Niagara Mohawk said, it notified the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission that transmission services would no longer be provided to these customers once the NYPA contract is terminated.

Because canceling the contract would leave 37 industrial customers without access to some or all of their NYPA electricity, Niagara Mohawk said, it has requested approval of a "bridge tariff," a commission-authorized rate that will allow the company to serve these customers at a price below what the customers are now paying NYPA.
The bridge tariff would remain in place until Niagara Mohawk's PowerChoice proposal becomes effective.
